hints: Build a cumulative frequency table by computing running totals of the shopper frequencies across each class interval.
Plot each cumulative frequency at the upper boundary of its interval: $(30, 16)$, $(50, 56)$, $(70, 104)$, $(90, 130)$, $(140, 160)$, starting at $(0, 0)$.
Use uniform linear scales: horizontal axis covering at least $0$ to $140$ dollars and vertical axis covering $0$ to $160$ cumulative frequency.
Connect the plotted points with a smooth curve or polygon through $(0, 0)$.
walkthrough:
Construct the cumulative frequency distribution table from the given frequency data:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Amount spent (\$x)} & \text{Frequency } f & \text{Cumulative Frequency } (cf) & \text{Plot Coordinate } (x, cf) \\
\hline
x \le 0 & 0 & 0 & (0, 0) \\
0 < x \le 30 & 16 & 16 & (30, 16) \\
30 < x \le 50 & 40 & 16 + 40 = 56 & (50, 56) \\
50 < x \le 70 & 48 & 56 + 48 = 104 & (70, 104) \\
70 < x \le 90 & 26 & 104 + 26 = 130 & (90, 130) \\
90 < x \le 140 & 30 & 130 + 30 = 160 & (140, 160) \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

Establish linear scales on both axes:
- Horizontal axis: Amount spent (\$), from $0$ to at least $140$.
- Vertical axis: Cumulative frequency (number of shoppers), from $0$ to at least $160$.
Plot the six coordinates $(0, 0)$, $(30, 16)$, $(50, 56)$, $(70, 104)$, $(90, 130)$, $(140, 160)$ and join them with a continuous smooth curve or polygon.
teacher_walkthrough:
Calculate the cumulative frequencies by adding each group's frequency to the running total:
$$\begin{aligned} t \le 30: & \quad 16 \\ t \le 50: & \quad 16 + 40 = 56 \\ t \le 70: & \quad 56 + 48 = 104 \\ t \le 90: & \quad 104 + 26 = 130 \\ t \le 140: & \quad 130 + 30 = 160 \end{aligned}$$
Plot each cumulative frequency against the upper boundary of its class interval: $(0,0), (30,16), (50,56), (70,104), (90,130), (140,160)$.
Join the plotted points with a smooth, continuous cumulative frequency curve.

hints: For total frequency $N = 160$, locate the median at cumulative frequency $0.5 \times 160 = 80$, the lower quartile $Q_1$ at $0.25 \times 160 = 40$, and the upper quartile $Q_3$ at $0.75 \times 160 = 120$.
Read horizontally from these cumulative frequencies to the curve, then vertically down to read the corresponding amounts on the spending axis.
Calculate the interquartile range using $\mathrm{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$.
walkthrough:
Find the median ($Q_2$) at cumulative frequency $\frac{1}{2} \times 160 = 80$:
$$\text{Reading from cumulative frequency } 80 \text{ to the graph gives: } \text{Median} \approx 59\text{ dollars (accept } 57\text{ to } 60\text{ dollars)}$$

Find the lower quartile ($Q_1$) and upper quartile ($Q_3$) from the graph:
$$\text{Position of } Q_1 = 0.25 \times 160 = 40 \implies Q_1 \approx 43\text{ dollars (accept } 41\text{ to } 44\text{)}$$
$$\text{Position of } Q_3 = 0.75 \times 160 = 120 \implies Q_3 \approx 82\text{ dollars (accept } 80\text{ to } 84\text{)}$$

Calculate the interquartile range (IQR):
$$\mathrm{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 \approx 82 - 43 = 39\text{ dollars (acceptable range: around } 37\text{ to } 41\text{ dollars)}$$
teacher_walkthrough: The median corresponds to half of the total 160 shoppers ($160 / 2 = 80$). Locate 80 on the vertical cumulative frequency axis and read across to the curve: the median is $\$59$.
The lower quartile ($Q_1$) is at a cumulative frequency of $160 / 4 = 40$. Reading across to the curve gives $Q_1 = \$43$.
The upper quartile ($Q_3$) is at a cumulative frequency of $3 \times 40 = 120$. Reading across to the curve gives $Q_3 = \$82$.

Subtract the lower quartile from the upper quartile to calculate the interquartile range:
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 82 - 43 = 39\text{ dollars}$$

hints: Locate $\$115$ on the horizontal axis and read up to the cumulative frequency curve to determine how many shoppers spent $\$115$ or less.
Subtract that cumulative frequency reading from the total of $160$ shoppers to find how many spent more than $\$115$.
walkthrough:
Read the cumulative frequency corresponding to an expenditure of $115$ dollars from the graph:
$$\text{Cumulative frequency at } \$115 \approx 149\text{ shoppers (acceptable range: } 144\text{ to } 151\text{)}$$

Subtract from the total number of shoppers ($160$) to determine those who spent more than $115$ dollars:
$$\text{Number spending } > \$115 = 160 - 149 = 11\text{ shoppers (acceptable range: } 9\text{ to } 16\text{)}$$
$$\text{Alternatively, by midpoint interpolation on } [90, 140]: \dfrac{30}{2} = 15\text{ shoppers}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Locate $\$115$ on the horizontal amount-spent axis and read up to the cumulative frequency curve: the cumulative frequency is 149 shoppers.

Subtract from the total of 160 shoppers to find how many spent more than $\$115$:
$$\text{Shoppers spending } > \$115 = 160 - 149 = 11\text{ shoppers}$$

hints: Estimate the mean of grouped continuous data using the midpoint of each class interval.
Compute the midpoints $x$ of the 5 intervals: $15$, $40$, $60$, $80$, and $115$.
Multiply each midpoint by its frequency, sum the products $\sum fx$, and divide by total frequency $160$.
walkthrough:
Determine the midpoints $x$ of each class interval by averaging lower and upper boundaries:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Class Interval} & \text{Midpoint } x & \text{Frequency } f & f x \\
\hline
0 < x \le 30 & \frac{0 + 30}{2} = 15 & 16 & 15 \times 16 = 240 \\
30 < x \le 50 & \frac{30 + 50}{2} = 40 & 40 & 40 \times 40 = 1600 \\
50 < x \le 70 & \frac{50 + 70}{2} = 60 & 48 & 60 \times 48 = 2880 \\
70 < x \le 90 & \frac{70 + 90}{2} = 80 & 26 & 80 \times 26 = 2080 \\
90 < x \le 140 & \frac{90 + 140}{2} = 115 & 30 & 115 \times 30 = 3450 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

Compute the total sum of products $\sum fx$:
$$\sum fx = 240 + 1600 + 2880 + 2080 + 3450 = 10250$$

Divide by total frequency $\sum f = 160$ to calculate the estimated mean amount spent:
$$\bar{x} = \dfrac{\sum fx}{\sum f} = \dfrac{10250}{160} = 64.0625 \approx 64.1\text{ dollars}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Find the midpoint of each price interval by averaging its lower and upper boundaries:
$$\text{Midpoints: } 15, 40, 60, 80, 115$$

Multiply each midpoint by the number of shoppers in that group, and sum them to get the total amount spent:
$$\sum fx = (15 \times 16) + (40 \times 40) + (60 \times 48) + (80 \times 26) + (115 \times 30) = 240 + 1600 + 2880 + 2080 + 3450 = 10250$$

Divide by the total of 160 shoppers to estimate the mean:
$$\text{Mean} = \frac{10250}{160} = 64.0625 \approx 64.1\text{ dollars}$$
